summary: Herodotus (5th century BCE) on the Atlantes of north-west Africa, who take their name from Mount Atlas, the "pillar of heaven". A real people and a real mountain, long before Plato; often confused with Atlantis.

tree.title: Herodotus 4.184: the Atarantes and Mount Atlas, whose people are the Atlantes
tree.summary: After the Garamantes come the Atarantes, who have no personal names, then a salt hill and the Atlas mountain, slender, round and cloud-capped. The people there, called Atlantes after the mountain, are said to eat no living thing and to see no dreams.

tree.title: Herodotus 4.185: the ridge of salt hills to the Pillars of Heracles
tree.summary: Herodotus says he can name the peoples of the ridge as far as the Atlantes and knows that the ridge reaches the Pillars of Heracles and beyond. He describes the salt-block houses and the rainless region of Libya beyond.
